{{Short description|Czech physicist}}
'''Petr Hořava''' (born 1963 in [[Prostějov]])<ref>[https://www.nfneuron.cz/cs/vedci/petr-horava Profile at Grant Fund Neuron website]</ref> is a [[Czechs|Czech]] [[superstring theory|string theorist]]. He is a professor of physics in the [[Berkeley Center for Theoretical Physics]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he teaches courses on [[quantum field theory]] and [[string theory]]. Hořava is a member of the theory group at [[LBNL|Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]].

==Work==
Hořava is known for his articles written with [[Edward Witten]] about the [[Hořava–Witten domain wall]]s in [[M-theory]]. These articles demonstrated that the ten-dimensional [[heterotic string|heterotic]] <math>E_8 \times E_8</math> string theory could be produced from 11-dimensional [[M-theory]] by making one of the dimensions have edges (the domain walls). This discovery provided crucial support for the conjecture that all string theories could arise as limits of a single higher-dimensional theory.

Hořava is less well known for his discovery of [[D-branes]], usually attributed to Jin Dai, [[Robert Leigh (physicist)|Robert Leigh]] and [[Joseph Polchinski]], who discovered them independently, also in 1989.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1016/0370-2693(89)90209-8 | title=Background duality of open-string models | year=1989 | last1=Hořava | first1=Petr | journal=Physics Letters B | volume=231 | issue=3 | pages=251–257 | bibcode=1989PhLB..231..251H }}</ref>

In 2009, Hořava proposed a [[Hořava–Lifshitz gravity|theory of gravity]] that separates space from time at high energy while matching some predictions of [[general relativity]] at lower energies.<ref>{{cite journal | arxiv=0901.3775 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.79.084008 | title=Quantum gravity at a Lifshitz point | year=2009 | last1=Hořava | first1=Petr | journal=Physical Review D | volume=79 | issue=8 | article-number=084008 | bibcode=2009PhRvD..79h4008H | s2cid=891685 }}</ref><ref>Zeeya Merali, "[http://www.scientificamerican.com/article.cfm?id=splitting-time-from-space Splitting Time from Space—New Quantum Theory Topples Einstein's Spacetime]", Scientific American (Dec. 2009).</ref>
